children: 0506 GMT - Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's comments complicate the AI trade, Tiger Brokers market strategist James Ooi says in a note. Warsh said at the Jackson Hole symposium that the Fed policy remains unrestrictive given rapid business capex growth, much of it AI-related. Investors now have to weigh whether capex growth could increase the odds of tighter monetary policy, Ooi says. Higher interest rates raise discount rates, weighing on AI hardware valuations, he adds. Asian tech hardware stocks fall after U.S. semiconductor shares declined following Warsh's hawkish speech on Friday. SK Hynix falls 2.5%, Samsung Electronics drops 1.95% and TSMC loses 1.45%. (sherry.qin@wsj.com)

0250 GMT - The Singapore dollar strengthens slightly against its U.S. counterpart on likely technical recovery after falling to a more than one-week low on Friday. Overbought conditions for the U.S. dollar-Singapore dollar pair suggest any advance for next 24 hours could be contained within a 1.2725-1.2765 range, two members of UOB Global Economics & Markets Research say in a report. Even if the U.S. dollar were to rise above S$1.2765, major resistance at S$1.2780 is unlikely to come into view, the members add. The U.S. dollar is 0.1% lower at S$1.2735 after touching S$1.2753 on Friday, its highest intraday level since Aug. 19, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)

0241 GMT - South Korea is set to post another month of solid chip-led export growth for August, with its trade surplus expected to top $30 billion for a third straight month. The median forecast from a Wall Street Journal poll of 13 economists is for a 62.0% on-year increase in shipments overseas, following a revised 63.0% rise in July. Imports are projected to have risen 22.4% on year, resulting in a $30.39 billion trade surplus in August. Overall export growth was likely driven by semiconductors and other IT products, while automobile exports stayed sluggish amid labor strikes in the sector, says iM Securities' Park Sang-hyun. The trade data are due Tuesday.(kwanwoo.jun@wsj.com)

0224 GMT - Bitcoin falls in Asian trading. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish speech at the Jackson Hole symposium on Friday boosted U.S. bond yields and the dollar, says IG market analyst Tony Sycamore in a note. Higher borrowing rates tend to weigh on risk appetite, dragging cryptocurrencies. Bitcoin falls 0.95% to $77,851.62, LSEG data show.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)

0208 GMT - The Thai baht and the Indonesian rupiah seem particularly exposed to the rise in Fed rate-hike prospects, MUFG Bank's Lloyd Chan says in a research report. "Thailand continues to offer limited yield support [to baht], while elevated Brent prices are weighing on the external balance," the senior currency analyst says. "For Indonesia, higher U.S. yields arrive as investors are increasingly monitoring domestic developments," Chan says. Recent protests in Indonesia have highlighted concerns about living costs and jobs, while approval ratings for the government have fallen, Chan notes. The dollar is 0.1% higher at 33.15 baht and 0.4% higher at 17,750 rupiah, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)

0140 GMT - JGBs fall in price terms in the early Tokyo session as the BOJ may face challenges in matching the pace of likely Fed rate hikes. "If the Fed steps up monetary tightening to curb inflation, the environment facing both the BOJ and the JGB market is likely to become more challenging," SMBC Nikko Securities' Ataru Okumura says in commentary. "What is currently being priced in is merely a faster pace of reducing the degree of monetary accommodation, rather than a shift toward outright monetary tightening" by the BOJ, the chief Japan rates strategist adds. The 10-year JGB yield is up 1.5 bps at 2.940% after earlier touching 2.950%, its highest intraday level since Sept. 1996. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)

0121 GMT - The market is pricing a more credible Fed in response to Fed Chairman Warsh's speech last Friday, three members of BofA Global Research say in a research report. "The [U.S.] yield curve flattened on the back of a sharp sell-off at the front end," the members note, citing market pricing of a Fed rate hike in September which is now over 60%. However, given Warsh's comments that the Fed should focus on trends rather than "isolated data points" and that underlying inflation hasn't "meaningfully improved" in recent months, the onus is now on Warsh to deliver a rate hike in September, the members add. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)

0021 GMT - Asian currencies consolidate against the dollar in early trade, but may weaken on growing prospects of Fed rate hikes that typically increase the appeal of U.S. fixed-income assets. Although Fed Chairman Warsh's speech on Friday isn't a "pre-commitment to a Sep hike, it reinforced the Fed's inflation-fighting credibility and kept further tightening in play if inflation fails to ease meaningfully," two strategists at OCBC Group Research say in a research report. "A firmer USD can be a headwind for Asian FX," they add. The dollar is little changed at 159.98 yen and is steady at 1,377.10 won, while the Australian dollar is flat at US$0.7160, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)

0014 GMT - Japanese stocks decline after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's speech on Friday increased prospects for U.S. rate increases. Chip-related stocks are leading declines. Advantest falls 7.8%, SoftBank Group is 4.2% lower and Tokyo Electron is down 3.8%. The dollar is at 160.00 yen, up from Y159.48 as of Friday's Tokyo stock market close. Investors are closely watching developments in the Iran war and oil prices after U.S. forces attacked two Iranian rocket launchers in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday. The Nikkei Stock Average is down 2.2% at 64930.03. (kosaku.narioka@wsj.com; @kosakunarioka)

0009 GMT - JGBs edge lower in the early Tokyo session, tracking Friday's price declines in U.S. Treasurys. Both JGBs and Treasurys tend to move in tandem. Fed Chairman Warsh's speech on Friday sparked a shift in U.S. monetary-policy expectations, analysts say. The implied probability of the Fed raising rates by 25 bps at its September meeting climbed to around 59%, up from about 35% just one day earlier, XS.com's Antonio Di Giacomo says in an email. "The move shows that investors are once again seriously considering a scenario in which the Fed may have to tighten monetary conditions further if inflation fails to show more convincing signs of slowing," the senior market analyst adds. The 10-year JGB yield is up 0.5 bps at 2.930%. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)

0003 GMT - The Reserve Bank of New Zealand is on track to deliver a second consecutive interest rates hike in September, taking the official cash rate to 2.75% on Wednesday, says Ben Jarman, economist at JP Morgan. With the policy rate still accommodative, and the data having cleared essentially every hurdle to demonstrate a growth pick-up, a 25bp hike is close to fully-priced, he adds. While business surveys initially stumbled following the oil supply shock, activity measures have since rebounded, he adds. (james.glynn@wsj.com; X @JamesGlynnWSJ)

2344 GMT - Japanese stocks may fall after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's speech on Friday raised expectations for U.S. rate increases. Nikkei futures are down 1.6% at 65480 on the SGX. The dollar is at 160.12 yen, up from Y159.48 as of Friday's Tokyo stock market close. Investors are focusing on government bond yields and developments in the Middle East. The Nikkei Stock Average rose 0.4% to 66405.56 on Friday. (kosaku.narioka@wsj.com)
